rows.question: What was the change in NAV during 2Q17 and what drove it?
rows.answer: In 2Q17, NAV increased from $7,954.2M to $8,065.4M [PSERS 2Q17 Page 20 p.20], driven by $246.4M of paid-in capital and $432.2M of net value change, partially offset by $567.4M of capital distributed [PSERS 2Q17 Page 20 p.20]. The top quarterly value drivers were Bridgepoint Europe IV (+$37.7M), New Mountain Partners III (+$34.6M), Baring Asia PE Fund IV (+$32.0M), CVC European Equity Partners V (+$30.4M), and Bridgepoint Europe III (+$22.9M), collectively contributing $157.6M or 28.7% of net value gain [PSERS 2Q17 Page 21 p.21]. The largest detractor was Platinum Equity Capital Partners II (-$34.6M), followed by Cerberus Institutional Partners V (-$9.1M) and Crestview Partners II (-$8.0M), totaling -$64.2M or 54.7% of net value loss [PSERS 2Q17 Page 21 p.21].
rows.judge_rationale: All figures cited (NAV bridge components and top/bottom drivers) are accurately drawn from the retrieved chunks, but several chunks (performance summary tables, vintage year diversification) are irrelevant to the NAV change question.

rows.question: What was the NAV change between 2Q17 and 3Q17 and the primary drivers?
rows.answer: The total portfolio NAV change in 3Q17 (quarter ended 09/30/2017) was a net value gain of $243.5M, representing a 3.06% quarterly IRR [PSERS 3Q17 Page 21 p.21]. The primary drivers of appreciation were Crestview Partners II (+$36.4M), CVC European Equity Partners V (+$22.9M), LLR Equity Partners IV (+$18.5M), Bain Capital Asia Fund III (+$16.4M), and Cinven Fifth Fund (+$14.9M), totaling $109.1M or 27.3% of net value gain [PSERS 3Q17 Page 21 p.21]. The primary detractors were Platinum Equity Capital Partners II (-$11.5M), Cinven Sixth Fund (-$9.7M), Actis Emerging Markets 3 (-$5.3M), Psilos Group Partners III (-$4.8M), and Baring Asia Private Equity Fund III (-$4.0M), totaling -$35.3M or 22.6% of net value loss; note that the negative figures for Bridgepoint Europe IV and Apax Europe VII-B were wholly due to a methodology change to reflect unrealized accrued carried interest [PSERS 3Q17 Page 21 p.21]. A prior-quarter (2Q17) NAV figure is not provided in the excerpts, so the absolute NAV change between 2Q17 and 3Q17 cannot be precisely calculated.

rows.question: Describe the valuation methodology applied to Level 3 investments in Q3 2025.
rows.answer: Level III equity investments ($7,030,763 thousand fair value) are primarily valued using Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) with WACC ranging 8.7%–31.1% (weighted-average 17.0%) and Exit Multiples of 6.5x–24.0x (weighted-average 16.3x), with smaller portions valued via Transactional Value ($877 thousand) and Recent Round of Financing ($272,865 thousand) [Blackstone PES Q3 2025 Item 1 — Financial Statements]. Private Debt investments ($846,537 thousand) use DCF with WACC of 8.3%–16.1% (weighted-average 12.7%), Liquid Debt ($2,311 thousand) uses Third-Party Pricing, and Affiliated Investee Funds ($81,668 thousand) use DCF with WACC of 7.1%–24.6% (weighted-average 14.7%) [Blackstone PES Q3 2025 Item 1 — Financial Statements]. Level III pricing inputs are unobservable and valuation considers factors including acquisition price, nature of investment, local market conditions, comparable company valuations, and current/projected operating performance [Blackstone PES Q3 2025 Item 1 — Financial Statements].

Investments at Fair Value and Investments in Affiliated or Unaffiliated Investee Funds
Investments at Fair Value
The Aggregator records public and private investments at trade date and closing date, respectively, and values its investments at fair value in accordance with ASC 820. Fair value is the amount that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability, in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. In the absence of observable market prices, the Aggregator’s investments are valued using valuation methodologies applied on a consistent basis as described below. Additional information regarding these investments is provided in Note 3. “Investments and Fair Value Measurement.”
The Aggregator’s determination of fair value is based on the best information available in the circumstances and incorporates the Aggregator’s own assumptions, including assumptions that the Aggregator believes market participants would use in valuing the investments, and involves a significant degree of judgment, taking into consideration a combination of internal and external factors, including appropriate risk adjustments for
non-performance
and liquidity.
